subject: Animation
title: Timing and Spacing: The Feel of Motion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Timing and Spacing: The Feel of Motion.

hook.text: Timing is how many frames an action takes. Spacing is how far an object moves between frames.

buildup.text: More frames make action slower and smoother. Fewer frames make it snappy and energetic.

discovery.text: Spacing creates the illusion of weight. Heavy objects have more frames. Light objects snap with fewer frames.

twist.text: The same character doing the same action can feel happy, sad, or angry based entirely on timing changes.

climax.text: Timing and spacing are what separate mechanical movement from animation that feels alive and emotional.

punchline.text: The same drawing can feel heavy or light depending on timing.

quiz.question: How do timing and spacing create the illusion of weight in animation?
options: Heavy objects use more frames with tighter spacing; light objects snap quickly with fewer frames
Weight is created by adding shadows to objects

details.summary: Timing is how long an action takes; spacing is how far objects move between frames. Together they determine whether movement feels heavy or light, fast or slow, smooth or abrupt — they are animation's most essential technical tools.
details.whyItMatters: Timing and spacing are what distinguish good animation from great animation. They control the physical and emotional feel of every movement, making them the most studied skills in professional animation.
takeaways: Timing determines how many frames an action occupies
Spacing determines how far objects move between each frame
Together they control the weight, speed, and feel of all movement

faq.question: How do timing and spacing create the illusion of weight?
faq.answer: Heavy objects have slow starts, fast acceleration, and hard stops with little bounce. Light objects accelerate quickly and decelerate gently. The frame count (timing) and distance per frame (spacing) encode this physical information.

faq.question: Can timing and spacing convey emotion as well as physics?
faq.answer: Absolutely. A sad character moves with slow timing and small spacing. An excited character has fast timing and wide spacing. Animators use the same tools for physical believability and emotional expression simultaneously.
